text:
Ivy: hi team, first week Q: i'm finishing my first PR but unsure about keeping WIP commits visible. should I leave the small "wip" commits or squash before requesting review? also what's our preferred PR title format?
Kaito: welcome! keep iterative commits while you work so reviews can follow your thought process, but squash or tidy up before merge so history is clean. if you want reviewers to see the incremental work, push and mark the PR draft.
Ruth: PR title: imperative, short, capitalized. Example: "Add safe retry for gateway calls". In the body include: summary, testing steps, and a short checklist (lint/tests/payloads).
Ivy: any guidance on commit message body length or including jira/ticket refs?
Kaito: include ticket ID in the PR title or first line if there is one. Commit messages should be one-line subject in imperative mood and optional body explaining why. Keep body lines <=72 chars.
Ruth: for small fixes you can squash into a single commit like: "fix(http): handle 504 from payment provider". For larger features keep logical commits but reorder/reword via interactive rebase before merge.
Ivy: what about branch naming? I've been using iv/feature-x, is that ok?
Kaito: prefer feature/<ticket>-short-desc or fix/<ticket>-short-desc. Personal prefixes are ok for short-lived branches but try to follow the pattern: feature/987-add-cache.
merge-bot: reminder: required checks -> lint, unit-tests, license-scan. PR cannot be merged until all pass.
Ruth: when you request review, add a short note what to focus on (API changes, performance, tests). If it touches infra or runtime, add @infra-team and request two reviewers.
Ivy: thanks! i'll clean up commits with rebase and open the PR as draft until tests pass. appreciate the help. :)
Kaito: welcome aboard — ping us for a quick walkthrough of the repo layout if helpful.
